findings.summary: closeMenu() removes the 'keydown' listener but never calls document.removeEventListener('click', onClickOutside), even though onClickOutside is added on every openMenu() call. The brief explicitly requires 'cleaning up any listeners added for the outside-click detection once the menu is closed, so they don't keep firing after the menu is dismissed' — this is the one concrete requirement in the brief, and it's unimplemented. Concretely: open the menu once, close it (Escape, toggle click, or an outside click) — the document-level click listener stays registered forever. Every subsequent click anywhere on the page (even in unrelated content, forms, etc.) now invokes onClickOutside, which unconditionally calls closeMenu() again, which calls toggleEl.focus() — silently yanking keyboard focus to the hamburger button on every click across the whole site after the mobile menu has been used once. Opening the menu multiple times stacks additional duplicate listeners (addEventListener with the same function reference and options is a no-op per spec, so it won't literally duplicate here, but the listener never being removed means the leak/focus-theft persists indefinitely for the life of the page).
